questions.title: Square Inherits Rectangle Area
questions.description:
Define a Rectangle class with width/height and an area method. Define Square as a subclass of Rectangle that overrides initialize to set both dimensions equal. Read one integer side, compute and print the square's area.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer side.

Output Format:
The integer area (side * side).

Constraints:
1 <= side <= 1000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Rectangle
  def initialize(w, h); @w = w; @h = h; end
  def area; @w * @h; end
end

class Square < Rectangle
  def initialize(s); super(s, s); end
end

s = gets.to_i
sq = Square.new(s)
puts sq.area

questions.title: Zoo Animal Hierarchy Sounds
questions.description:
A zoo app models animals. Define a base Animal class with name and a sound method. Define subclasses Lion, Tiger, and Elephant, each overriding sound to return '<name> roars', '<name> growls', '<name> trumpets' respectively. Read n then n lines each containing a kind and a name; print the sound of each animal on its own line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'kind name' (kind is lion, tiger, or elephant).

Output Format:
One sound per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= name length <= 30.
questions.sampleinput1:
3
lion Leo
tiger Tony
elephant Dumbo
questions.sampleoutput1:
Leo roars
Tony growls
Dumbo trumpets
questions.input2:
4
tiger a
lion b
tiger c
elephant d
questions.output2:
a growls
b roars
c growls
d trumpets
questions.whitelist: class Lion, class Tiger, class Elephant
questions.sourcecode:
class Animal
  def initialize(name); @name = name; end
  def sound; "#{@name} makes a sound"; end
end

class Lion < Animal
  def sound; "#{@name} roars"; end
end

class Tiger < Animal
  def sound; "#{@name} growls"; end
end

class Elephant < Animal
  def sound; "#{@name} trumpets"; end
end

n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  kind, name = gets.split
  obj = case kind
  when "lion" then Lion.new(name)
  when "tiger" then Tiger.new(name)
  when "elephant" then Elephant.new(name)
  end
  puts obj.sound
end

Define a Manager subclass that calls super in initialize to set name/salary, then stores team size; it overrides bonus to return super * 2 and overrides report to call super and append ':<team>'. Read n then for each manager read name, salary, team; print each report on its own line.

Line 1: integer n. Next n groups of 3 lines: name, salary, team.

Output Format:
One report per line: '<name>:<bonus>:<team>'.

questions.title: Private Pin Verification Account
questions.description:
A bank's account keeps its PIN private. Define an Account class storing owner and pin. The public verify method compares the entered PIN against the value returned by a private method hidden_pin and returns 'Access granted for <owner>' or 'Access denied for <owner>'. Read owner, pin, and entered pin; print the verification result.

Input Format:
Line 1: owner. Line 2: integer correct pin. Line 3: integer entered pin.

Output Format:
'Access granted for <owner>' or 'Access denied for <owner>'.

Constraints:
1 <= owner length <= 30; 0 <= pin <= 9999.
questions.sourcecode:
class Account
  def initialize(owner, pin); @owner = owner; @pin = pin; end
  def verify(input)
    if input == hidden_pin
      "Access granted for #{@owner}"
    else
      "Access denied for #{@owner}"
    end
  end
  private
  def hidden_pin; @pin; end
end

owner = gets.chomp
pin = gets.to_i
input = gets.to_i
a = Account.new(owner, pin)
puts a.verify(input)

questions.title: Shape Area Override Chain Aggregator
questions.description:
A geometry tool models shapes. Define a Shape base class whose area method returns 0. Define Circle (area = 3 * r * r using 3 for pi), Rectangle (area = w * h), and Square as a subclass of Rectangle that calls super(s, s) in initialize. Read n then n lines describing a shape ('circle r', 'rect w h', or 'square s'); compute and print the sum of all areas as an integer.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: shape descriptor with dimensions.

Output Format:
Integer total area.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= r, w, h, s <= 100.
questions.whitelist: class Circle, class Rectangle, class Square, def area
questions.sourcecode:
class Shape
  def area; 0; end
end

class Circle < Shape
  def initialize(r); @r = r; end
  def area; 3 * @r * @r; end
end

class Rectangle < Shape
  def initialize(w, h); @w = w; @h = h; end
  def area; @w * @h; end
end

class Square < Rectangle
  def initialize(s); super(s, s); end
end

n = gets.to_i
total = 0
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  kind = parts[0]
  shape = case kind
  when "circle" then Circle.new(parts[1].to_i)
  when "rect" then Rectangle.new(parts[1].to_i, parts[2].to_i)
  when "square" then Square.new(parts[1].to_i)
  end
  total += shape.area
end
puts total

questions.title: Bank Branch Counter With Subclasses
questions.description:
A bank tracks accounts across account types. Define a Bank base class with @@accounts and @@total_balance starting at 0. The constructor takes a balance and increments both class variables. Define class methods self.accounts, self.total_balance, and self.average (returns 0 when @@accounts is 0, otherwise integer division). Define Savings and Checking subclasses whose constructors call super(balance). Read n then n lines 'type balance' (type is S for savings, C for checking); print three lines: 'Accounts: <n>', 'Total: <total>', 'Avg: <avg>'.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'type balance' (type in S, C).

Output Format:
Three lines as described.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 100; 0 <= balance <= 1000000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Bank
  @@accounts = 0
  @@total_balance = 0
  def initialize(balance); @balance = balance; @@accounts += 1; @@total_balance += balance; end
  def self.accounts; @@accounts; end
  def self.total_balance; @@total_balance; end
  def self.average; @@accounts.zero? ? 0 : @@total_balance / @@accounts; end
end

class Savings < Bank
  def initialize(balance); super(balance); end
  def type; "Savings"; end
end

class Checking < Bank
  def initialize(balance); super(balance); end
  def type; "Checking"; end
end

n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  kind = parts[0]
  bal = parts[1].to_i
  if kind == "S"
    Savings.new(bal)
  else
    Checking.new(bal)
  end
end
puts "Accounts: #{Bank.accounts}"
puts "Total: #{Bank.total_balance}"
puts "Avg: #{Bank.average}"

questions.title: Protected Balance Cross Instance Compare
questions.description:
A leaderboard compares balances between two accounts using a protected method. Define an Account class with owner and balance. Define a public richer_than?(other) that returns balance > other.balance where balance is a protected method returning @balance. Define a public report(other) that returns '<owner> richer' if richer_than?(other) is true, else '<owner> not richer'. Read owner_a, balance_a, owner_b, balance_b; instantiate two Account objects and print a.report(b).

Input Format:
Line 1: owner_a. Line 2: integer balance_a. Line 3: owner_b. Line 4: integer balance_b.

Output Format:
'<owner_a> richer' or '<owner_a> not richer'.

Constraints:
1 <= owner length <= 30; 0 <= balance <= 1000000.
questions.sourcecode:
class Account
  def initialize(owner, balance); @owner = owner; @balance = balance; end
  def richer_than?(other); balance > other.balance; end
  def report(other); richer_than?(other) ? "#{@owner} richer" : "#{@owner} not richer"; end
  protected
  def balance; @balance; end
end

a_name = gets.chomp
a_bal = gets.to_i
b_name = gets.chomp
b_bal = gets.to_i
a = Account.new(a_name, a_bal)
b = Account.new(b_name, b_bal)
puts a.report(b)

questions.title: Premium Tier Super Chain Describe
questions.description:
A bank has a multi-tier Premium account. Define a base Account class with owner and a describe method returning 'Account[<owner>]'. Define Savings subclass that calls super(owner) in initialize, stores rate, and overrides describe to call super and append ' Savings[<rate>%]'. Define Premium subclass of Savings that calls super(owner, rate) in initialize, stores tier, and overrides describe to call super and append ' Premium[<tier>]'. Read n then n lines 'owner rate tier'; print each Premium account's describe on its own line.

Input Format:
Line 1: integer n. Next n lines: 'owner rate tier' (rate integer, tier single word).

Output Format:
One describe per line.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= owner length <= 30; 0 <= rate <= 20; 1 <= tier length <= 20.
questions.sampleoutput1:
Account[Alice] Savings[5%] Premium[Gold]
Account[Bob] Savings[3%] Premium[Silver]
questions.input2:
3
A 2 X
B 3 Y
C 4 Z
questions.output2:
Account[A] Savings[2%] Premium[X]
Account[B] Savings[3%] Premium[Y]
Account[C] Savings[4%] Premium[Z]
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 50; 1 <= owner length <= 30; 0 <= rate <= 20; 1 <= tier length <= 20
questions.sourcecode:
class Account
  def initialize(owner); @owner = owner; end
  def describe; "Account[#{@owner}]"; end
end

class Savings < Account
  def initialize(owner, rate); super(owner); @rate = rate; end
  def describe; super + " Savings[#{@rate}%]"; end
end

class Premium < Savings
  def initialize(owner, rate, tier); super(owner, rate); @tier = tier; end
  def describe; super + " Premium[#{@tier}]"; end
end

n = gets.to_i
n.times do
  parts = gets.split
  p = Premium.new(parts[0], parts[1].to_i, parts[2])
  puts p.describe
end
